facts.value: Sikhism is a panentheistic religion founded on the teachings of Guru Nanak and ten successive Sikh gurus in 15th-century Punjab.
Sikhism is the fifth-largest organized religion in the world, with approximately 30 million Sikhs.
Sikhs are expected to embody the qualities of a Sant-Sipāhī—a saint-soldier, have control over one's internal vices, and be constantly immersed in virtues clarified in the Guru Granth Sahib.
The principal belief of Sikhi is faith in Waheguru—represented by the phrase ik ōaṅkār, one cosmic divine actioner (God), who prevails in everything.
Sikhs are enjoined to engage in social reform through the pursuit of justice for all human beings.
